Name: UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) — 2030 Agenda
Lead_Body: [INT-O-032] UN General Assembly
Key_Commitments: 17 global goals adopted unanimously in Sept 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Directly relevant to climate-nature: SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 14 (Life Below Water), SDG 15 (Life on Land), SDG 6 (Clean Water), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 7 (Affordable Clean Energy). 169 targets and 232 indicators. UK committed to all 17 goals in EIP 2025. Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) report on progress.
UK_Engagement: UK committed; Defra leads UK reporting; EIP 2025 aligns to SDGs; UK VNR published 2019, 2022
UK_Links: [POL-001] Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; [POL-003] UK National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs); [POL-029] 2030 Strategic Framework for International Climate and Nature Action

Name: IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) 2021–2022
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Lead_Body: [INT-O-002] IPCC — Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
Key_Commitments: Most comprehensive assessment of climate science to date. WGI (physical science, 2021): '>1.1°C warming since pre-industrial; 1.5°C likely breached by early 2030s; every fraction of degree matters.' WGII (impacts, 2022): ~3.3–3.6bn people highly vulnerable to climate change; nature is under increasing pressure from climate change. WGIII (mitigation, 2022): rapid and deep emissions reductions needed in all sectors; NbS can contribute 10–30% of needed mitigation. Cross-chapter paper on biodiversity hotspots. The AR6-cycle ocean and cryosphere assessment is covered in detail by the IPCC SROCC [INT-P-032].
UK_Engagement: IPCC AR6 cited in CCC Progress Reports; informs UK CCRA3; Met Office contributed as lead author organisation
UK_Links: [ORG-003] Climate Change Committee (CCC); [ORG-017] Met Office; [ORG-002] DESNZ (Dept for Energy Security and Net Zero); [POL-025] UK National Climate Science Partnership (UKNCSP); IPCC AR6 / Cross-chapter Papers
Intl_Links: [INT-P-032] IPCC Special Report on the Ocean and Cryosphere in a Changing Climate (SROCC) 2019

Name: IPBES Global Assessment on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services 2019
Lead_Body: [INT-O-006] IPBES — Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
Key_Commitments: First global assessment of biodiversity and ecosystem services. Key findings: 1 million species threatened with extinction; ecosystems are deteriorating at unprecedented rates; the five direct drivers of change are (in order): land/sea use change, direct exploitation, climate change, pollution, invasive species. Introduced Nature's Contributions to People (NCP) framework. Evidence base for Kunming-Montreal GBF.
UK_Engagement: Cited in UK NBSAP, EIP and State of Nature reports; JNCC, NE and UK academics contributed as authors
UK_Links: [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [POL-003] UK National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; State of Nature 2023; IPBES Global Assessment

Name: IPBES Invasive Alien Species Assessment 2023
Lead_Body: [INT-O-006] IPBES — Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
Key_Commitments: First global assessment of invasive alien species (IAS). Found >37,000 alien species established worldwide; >3,500 are harmful IAS. IAS implicated in 60% of global extinctions. Economic costs >$423bn/year. Key messages: prevention is 100x cheaper than management; IAS are increasing. Direct input to GBF Target 6 (reduce IAS introduction rate by 50%). Informs UK INNS indicators (JNCC B6) and EIF H1–H2.
UK_Engagement: Informs UK INNS indicators and biosecurity strategy; UKCEH and JNCC scientists contributed
UK_Links: [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [POL-034] Plant Biosecurity Strategy for Great Britain (2023–2028); [ORG-020] Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA); [POL-003] UK National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025

Name: IPBES-IPCC Workshop Report: Biodiversity and Climate Change (2021)
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Lead_Body: [INT-O-023] IPBES-IPCC Joint Work Programme
Key_Commitments: Landmark joint scientific report exploring the links between biodiversity and climate change. Key findings: addressing climate change and biodiversity loss together is essential; 30–50% of Earth's land, freshwater and ocean area needs effective conservation and restoration to address both crises simultaneously; nature-based solutions can contribute significantly to climate mitigation; biodiversity is critical for ecosystem resilience to climate change.
UK_Engagement: Cited in CCC reports, NBSAP and EIP; UK scientists contributed (Met Office, UKCEH, JNCC)

Name: GBF Monitoring Framework and Indicator Framework
Year_Status: Adopted CBD COP15 Dec 2022; being operationalised 2023–2030
Lead_Body: CBD Secretariat / UNEP-WCMC (indicator portal)
Key_Commitments: Official monitoring framework for the Kunming-Montreal GBF. Three tiers: 21 headline indicators (e.g., Red List Index, Living Planet Index), 98 component indicators, and complementary indicators. Name: UNFCCC Global Stocktake (GST)
Year_Status: First GST concluded COP28 Dubai 2023; next GST 2028
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Lead_Body: [INT-O-001] UNFCCC — Conference of the Parties (COP)
Key_Commitments: Mechanism under Paris Agreement (Art. 14) to assess collective progress every 5 years. First GST (2021–2023) concluded: current NDCs insufficient; world not on track for 1.5°C; calls for tripling renewables and doubling energy efficiency by 2030; first explicit call to transition away from fossil fuels; nature-based solutions highlighted. Outcomes intended to inform updated NDCs due in 2025.
UK_Engagement: UK NDC updated Feb 2025 in response to GST outcomes; CCC advises government on NDC ambition
UK_Links: [ORG-003] Climate Change Committee (CCC); [ORG-002] DESNZ (Dept for Energy Security and Net Zero); Paris Agreement / UK NDC (2035: −81% vs 1990)

Name: UN SEEA EA — System of Environmental-Economic Accounting Ecosystem Accounting
Year_Status: Adopted UN Statistical Commission 2021 (international statistical standard)
Lead_Body: UN Committee of Experts on Environmental-Economic Accounting (UNCEEA)
Key_Commitments: International statistical standard adopted by UN for measuring and reporting on ecosystems and their services in physical and monetary terms. Covers: ecosystem extent accounts, ecosystem condition accounts, ecosystem service flow accounts, and monetary ecosystem asset accounts. Basis for national natural capital accounts including the UK ONS Natural Capital Accounts. Aligns with CBD GBF monitoring framework.
UK_Engagement: ONS UK Natural Capital Accounts follow SEEA EA; ONS is leading implementer; Defra and ONS contribute to international SEEA work
UK_Links: ONS Natural Capital Accounts; [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs); [POL-026] Natural Capital and Ecosystem Assessment (NCEA) Programme; SEEA EA (UN Ecosystem Accounts)

Lead_Body: Government of France and UK (co-founders); over 119 member countries
Key_Commitments: Multi-country coalition championing an ambitious post-2020 global biodiversity framework, particularly the 30×30 target. UK was a co-founder and champion. Name: WWF Living Planet Report (biennial)
Lead_Body: WWF International / Zoological Society of London (ZSL)
Key_Commitments: Biennial flagship publication tracking the state of nature globally. Produces the Living Planet Index (LPI) — a measure of the average change in population size of vertebrate species. LPI 2024: average decline of 73% in monitored wildlife populations since 1970. Also covers biodiversity finance gaps, planetary boundaries and nature-climate connections. LPI is a headline GBF indicator (H5).

UK_Links: [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); JNCC UK Biodiversity Indicators; [POL-003] UK National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025

Name: Planetary Boundaries Framework (Stockholm Resilience Centre)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Climate | Governance, Society & Data
Lead_Body: Stockholm Resilience Centre / Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research
Key_Commitments: Scientific framework identifying nine planetary boundaries within which humanity can safely operate. 2023 update: six boundaries crossed — biosphere integrity (biodiversity loss), climate change, land system change, freshwater change, novel entities (chemicals/plastics), biogeochemical flows (nitrogen/phosphorus). Remaining three (stratospheric ozone depletion, aerosol loading, ocean acidification) not yet transgressed. Increasingly influential in policy discussions on safe operating space.
UK_Engagement: Cited in CCC and UK climate-nature policy debates; Stockholm Resilience Centre collaborates with UK universities
UK_Links: [ORG-003] Climate Change Committee (CCC); [POL-025] UK National Climate Science Partnership (UKNCSP); [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs)

Name: European Green Deal — Biodiversity Strategy 2030 and Farm to Fork Strategy
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Climate
Lead_Body: [INT-O-031] European Commission
Key_Commitments: EU's ambitious strategy for a sustainable and green recovery. Biodiversity Strategy 2030: protect 30% of EU land and sea; restore 20% of degraded ecosystems by 2030; reduce pesticide use by 50%; reduce fertiliser use by 20%; convert 25% of farmland to organic by 2030. Farm to Fork: sustainable food system transformation. EU Nature Restoration Law (adopted 2024): legally binding targets to restore 20% of EU land and sea by 2030. Post-Brexit UK monitors closely as a trade partner.

Year_Status: CBD COP16 established Cali Fund (Oct 2024); ongoing

Key_Commitments: Multilateral benefit-sharing mechanism for the monetary benefits from commercial use of Digital Sequence Information (DSI) on genetic resources. Established at CBD COP16 Cali 2024 — landmark ABS mechanism. 50% of fund for conservation and indigenous peoples; 50% for developing country implementation. Separate from GEF and broader GBF finance mobilisation. Operates under Nagoya Protocol framework. Expected to generate significant finance for GBF Target 19.

Name: UNEP Emissions Gap Report (annual)
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Lead_Body: [INT-O-010] UNEP — UN Environment Programme
Key_Commitments: Annual flagship report assessing the gap between projected GHG emissions with current policies vs NDC pledges vs pathways consistent with 1.5°C and 2°C. 2024 report: world on track for ~2.6–3.1°C warming with current policies; even with full NDC implementation only 2.6°C. Lead_Body: [INT-O-010] UNEP — UN Environment Programme
Key_Commitments: Annual report tracking finance flows to nature-based solutions (NbS). 2023 report: NbS finance must triple to $542bn/year by 2030 to meet climate, biodiversity and land degradation goals; current flows $200bn/year; harmful finance flows $7 trillion/year. Key benchmark for GBF Target 19 ($200bn mobilisation). Informs TNFD, GBF finance negotiations and UK Green Finance Strategy.

UK_Links: [POL-012] Green Finance Strategy 2023; [POL-029] 2030 Strategic Framework for International Climate and Nature Action; ENCORE / TNFD Framework

Name: TNFD — Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures Framework (v1.0)
Year_Status: 2023; final recommendations published September 2023; voluntary adoption tracking from 2024; 400+ adopters by mid-2024
Lead_Body: TNFD Taskforce (40 senior executives from finance and corporates; co-chaired by Elizabeth Mrema and David Craig); secretariat hosted at UNEP-FI / WWF
Key_Commitments: Provides a global voluntary framework for organisations to identify, assess, manage and disclose nature-related dependencies, impacts, risks and opportunities. Based on four TCFD-aligned pillars (governance, strategy, risk management, metrics and targets). Core LEAP approach (Locate, Evaluate, Assess, Prepare). Includes 14 recommended disclosures and core metrics aligned with GBF Target 15. Sector-specific guidance released for food and agriculture, mining, financial institutions, and others. Incorporated into EU CSRD reporting (ESRS E4). UK Green Finance Strategy 2023 commits to exploring TNFD implementation; ENCORE framework is a complementary tool for assessing dependencies on ecosystem services.
Geographic_Extent: Global (voluntary); integration into EU CSRD (mandatory for large EU companies); UK Green Finance Strategy 2023
UK_Engagement: UK Government funded TNFD development (£4.8m 2021–2025); UK Green Finance Strategy 2023 commits to exploring TNFD adoption; Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 requires UK regulators to give 'due regard' to nature; ENCORE framework (UNEP-WCMC) is the data tool underpinning TNFD metrics
UK_Links: ENCORE / TNFD Framework (in biodiversity indicators spreadsheet); UK Green Finance Strategy 2023

Calls for climate-proof infrastructure, sustainable urban planning, and nature-based solutions for adaptation. Promotes the European Climate Risk Assessment (EUCRA 2024). Name: IPCC Special Report on the Ocean and Cryosphere in a Changing Climate (SROCC) 2019
Year_Status: 2019 (third special report of the AR6 cycle)
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Lead_Body: [INT-O-002] IPCC - Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (Working Groups I & II)
Key_Commitments: Comprehensive assessment of climate-change impacts on the ocean, polar regions, mountains and the cryosphere. Approved at IPCC-51, Monaco, 24 Sept 2019; 104 authors from 36 countries; over 6,900 references. Key findings: ocean warming has more than doubled since 1993; near-certain continued sea-level rise (revised upward); intensifying marine heatwaves; ocean deoxygenation and acidification; widespread sea-ice, glacier and permafrost loss; declining Arctic sea ice and snow cover; shifts in marine species distributions and fisheries potential. Underpins marine and coastal adaptation planning and the science base for ocean-related elements of the GBF and SDG 14.
UK_Engagement: UK contributed authors; informs UK CCRA marine/coastal chapters and the UK Marine Strategy; cited in MCCIP evidence and CCC advice
UK_Links: [ORG-003] Climate Change Committee (CCC); [ORG-017] Met Office; [POL-025] UK National Climate Science Partnership (UKNCSP); [POL-049] Marine Climate Change Impacts Partnership (MCCIP); UK Marine Strategy (UKMS); [POL-028] UK Marine Strategy (UKMS) 2025 — Programme of Measures

Key_Commitments: Global framework mobilising ocean science to deliver 'the science we need for the ocean we want.' Coordinates endorsed Decade Actions/Programmes around ten challenges (incl. ocean-climate nexus, marine pollution, sustainable ocean observing, a digital twin of the ocean). Directly supports SDG 14 (Life Below Water) and underpins observing systems feeding climate and marine-biodiversity assessment.
